subject: Service reachability advisory — regional request routing + canary fallback
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@acme-retail.com>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Service reachability advisory — regional request routing + canary fallback

Hi Sanjay,

We wanted to update you proactively: between 07:10–07:50 UTC this morning our telemetry flagged elevated request failures and increased latency originating from the eu-central cloud egress path that impacts tenant routing for EU-bound traffic (you may have seen 502/503 spikes and higher p99 latency). Our engineering team has identified a peering saturation issue on the downstream provider that is intermittently dropping connections to a subset of EU edge POPs.

What we have done so far:
- Automated routing now favors the nearest healthy POP in the same region; affected requests are being rehomed where possible.
- We’ve opened an emergency ticket with the provider and implemented an interim canary policy that routes traffic to an alternative egress cluster while we validate capacity.

Immediate ask for Acme Retail:
1) If you can, switch your tenant preference to the EU-regional fallback endpoint we provided earlier (endpoint-eu-fallback.redwood.ai) for the next 2–4 hours to reduce error surface.
2) Share traces for any persistent failures to ops+acme@acme-retail.com — that helps us correlate.

We know routing changes are disruptive; our goal is to keep your requests served with minimal degradation while the provider stabilization completes. Vanessa is on the call with the provider and will follow up with verification steps you can run to confirm connectivity.

I’m moving this thread into my inbox for the follow-up; please ping me directly if this is causing major impact to customer-facing SLAs.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-postmortem-draft-rl-0432.pdf (postmortem draft — internal)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Sanjay Patel <sanjay@acme-retail.com>
Cc: naomi.feldman@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service reachability advisory — regional request routing + canary fallback

Hi all,

Quick technical summary and reproducibility checks for Acme:
- Root cause: downstream peer reported a partial BGP flap combined with a queuing regression; packets to three EU edge racks experienced drops when load crossed a threshold.
- Mitigation performed: we incrementally shifted 40% of EU traffic to the regional fallback cluster (same AZs but different physical egress links) and throttled large-burst traffic agents to avoid amplifying the queue.

Steps for Acme to validate (can be done in parallel):
1) Curl health check against endpoint-eu-fallback.redwood.ai/health — expect 200 within 150ms.
2) Run a 1-minute synthetic load at small concurrency (10 qps) and capture first/last-request trace ids — send those to ops+acme@acme-retail.com.
3) If you need to keep production steady without changing client endpoint, set a routing header X-Redwood-Pref: fallback in requests for a canary subset (we can coordinate a token).

Planned next steps:
- 09:30 UTC: provider escalated to tier-2 networking team (already started).
- 10:00 UTC: we’ll re-evaluate whether to expand fallback to 70% or revert depending on provider updates.

If you see consistent 502s after these checks, include the request id and timestamp in the email; Naomi will correlate at the gateway.

-Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: acme-mtraces-20270418.zip (customer-sent traces)
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@acme-retail.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+acme@acme-retail.com
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 11:07:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Service reachability advisory — regional request routing + canary fallback

Thanks Marcus and Vanessa — appreciate the quick heads-up.

We ran the curl health check (200/120ms) and a 60s synthetic at 15 qps; attached are three trace ids where we still saw intermittent 503s (timestamps and request ids included). We switched ~30% of our traffic to the fallback endpoint as suggested and saw error rates drop by ~75% for the affected API surface.

One ask from our side: can Redwood share the canary token and a short window when you’ll be expanding fallback? We want to coordinate our feature flags to avoid double-routing. Also, we’ll need a short note for our on-call rotation (what to tell our NOC) — a 1–2 line summary would be great.

Sanjay
Sanjay Patel
Principal Engineer, Platform
Acme Retail
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@acme-retail.com>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, naomi.feldman@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 16:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service reachability advisory — regional request routing + canary fallback

Sanjay, thanks — great validation and thanks for the traces. Short answers and actions: 

- Canary token: token-acme-rl-20270419 (valid for 6 hours). Send that in header X-Redwood-Canary: token-acme-rl-20270419. We’ll gate to a subset of your tenant traffic (you control % via feature flag).
- Expansion window: we plan to evaluate at 18:00 UTC. If the provider reports stable BGP adjacencies and our egress metrics stay within normal bounds we’ll expand fallback to 65% for 2 hours, then fully normalize if graphs look stable. We’ll confirm via this thread before expanding.
- NOC blurb (1–2 lines): "Redwood is routing affected EU-bound requests to an alternative regional egress cluster due to downstream peering instability; errors should subside while routing is in fallback. Contact Redwood SRE if you observe persistent 5xx errors with request ids."

I’ve attached the internal postmortem draft; we’ll share a customer-facing summary after we finalize root cause and timeline. Naomi/Ben — please add any additional operational notes or rollback criteria you want included in the customer summary.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
